clue.text: I do various moves holding power weights

indicators.note: holding says the shuffled letters keep another piece within them
moves says the letters of the words before it are shifted into a new order

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone shuffling heavy weights around while showing off their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges I DO VARIOUS, and 'holding' puts P inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoirdupois is the traditional system of weights using pounds and ounces.

clue.text: Sailors had reportedly run off

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors; to be had is to be tricked, so had means conned

explanation.surface: Sailors were said to have deserted their ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, ABS CONNED sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to leave secretly and quickly, typically to escape capture or duty.

clue.text: Ordinary, unfinished abstract works

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
something unfinished is done only in part, partial

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses some abstract pieces as ordinary and incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s style of abstract painting built on optical illusions.

clue.text: Oriole regularly produces eggs

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the bird's name is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A songbird laying eggs at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs carried by a female fish.

clue.text: Education centre supported by variable software system

indicators.note: in a down answer, supported by puts the second piece underneath the first

parts.note: a uni (university) is a centre of higher education
X is the classic algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A college whose computers run on a particular operating system.
explanation.definitionFit: Unix is a long-established multi-user operating system for computers.

clue.text: Extra meeting with manager is up in the air

parts.note: something extra or surplus is left over
a head is the person in charge, a manager

explanation.surface: An additional meeting with the boss leaves everything uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in the air' looks like 'undecided' but is meant literally: above one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead describes something located aloft, above you, literally up in the air.

clue.text: Stubborn, small pet

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pet is a fit of sulking, a petty quarrel or tiff

explanation.surface: A description of an obstinate little animal kept at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' is not an animal but a fit of pique, as in 'in a pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff can mean unbending or obstinate, as in stiff opposition.

clue.text: Rejection of some teeny donations is unlikely to cause offence

indicators.note: Rejection says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Turning down tiny gifts is a harmless gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase standing in for an adjective: something anodyne is unlikely to cause offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means bland and inoffensive, deliberately avoiding controversy.

clue.text: Essentially skilled in ABCs, kid somehow reverted to making mistakes

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are combined in some new order
essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word skilled

explanation.surface: A child good at the alphabet slipped back into errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes L, the middle of 'skilled', which joins ABCS and KID in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into bad habits or former faults.

clue.text: In America, say, chief journalist is retiring

parts.note: to say is to state

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ED is the editor, the chief journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A senior newspaper editor is retiring to live in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' reads like a location for the story, but it is the definition; 'say' is a verb, not 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside is an informal adverb meaning in or towards the United States.

clue.text: I'm past the final stage?

parts.note: ago means in the past, earlier

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they have gone beyond the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: an insect's last stage of development.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the adult form of an insect, reached after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Decide not to take part in work with unscrupulous seller

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
a tout sells tickets at inflated prices

explanation.surface: Refusing to do business with a dodgy ticket seller.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose to withdraw from a scheme or activity.

clue.text: Dancing until dark

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the word until is rearranged

explanation.surface: People dancing until nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlit room has no lamp burning, so it is dark.

clue.text: Help for creating CV on a computer?

definitions.text: Help for creating CV on a computer?

parts.words: Help for creating CV on a computer?
parts.note: CV here is just two capital letters, which a keyboard key held down produces, not a résumé

explanation.walkthrough: CV looks like a curriculum vitae, but the clue means simply typing those two letters in upper case.
explanation.definitionFit: This keyboard key is held to type capital letters such as C and V.

clue.text: Corrupt, gutless duke accepts being rebuffed

indicators.note: accepts says the remaining letters take another piece inside
gutless means the inside letters of duke are removed, leaving its outside
rebuffed means pushed back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: being means existence, life

explanation.surface: A cowardly nobleman takes bribes after being snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' leaves DE of duke; 'rebuffed' turns LIFE into EFIL, which DE 'accepts'.
explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to spoil or pollute something pure, a verb sense of corrupt.

clue.text: Felt frequently unwell, thrashing about

indicators.note: frequently here means taking letters at regular intervals, the odd ones

parts.note: ailing means sick, unwell

explanation.surface: Someone who often felt ill, tossing and turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Flailing means waving the arms or body about wildly and without control.

clue.text: Pasta is to come down in price

indicators.note: in puts the first piece within the price word

parts.note: a fare is the price of a journey
to fall is to come down

explanation.surface: A shopper hears that pasta is about to get cheaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Farfalle is bow-tie or butterfly-shaped pasta, from the Italian for butterflies.

clue.text: Great, extremely labyrinthine story

parts.note: fab is slang for fabulous, great

indicators.note: extremely says take the extremes, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Praise for a wonderfully convoluted tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short tale, often with animals, that conveys a moral.

clue.text: They sell booze and repackaged TV dinners (unopened)

indicators.note: repackaged says the letters are boxed up again in a new order
unopened says the opening letter of dinners is taken off

explanation.surface: Ready meals put back in their packets, sold with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the D of DINNERS; 'repackaged' rearranges TV with INNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintners are wine merchants, who deal in alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Revolutionary insurrection after a strike — it's a shambles

indicators.note: after says the insurrection piece is placed following the opening pieces

parts.note: to bat is to hit or strike

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a riot is a violent public uprising

explanation.surface: An uprising follows a walk-out and everything is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' looks like a mess but has its old meaning: a slaughterhouse. 'strike' is a hit, not a walk-out.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles was originally a meat market or slaughterhouse, which is what an abattoir is.

clue.text: Drug aiming to eliminate the onset of gout

indicators.note: to eliminate says a letter is removed from the word before it

parts.note: to be aspiring is to be aiming high

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A medication intended to stop gout before it starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eliminate' removes G, picked by 'the onset of' gout.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling and anti-inflammatory medicine.

clue.text: I wait for minutes in the same place

parts.note: to bide is to wait, as in bide one's time

explanation.surface: Someone waits a few minutes without moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin used in references to mean in the same source as cited before.

clue.text: Shot of pool featuring occasional touches of this artist

indicators.note: featuring says the shot word includes the next piece

parts.note: a massé is a shot in pool or billiards played with a steeply angled cue

indicators.note: occasional touches means only some letters, taken at intervals, the odd ones

explanation.surface: A painting of a pool shot with a few strokes in this painter's style.
explanation.walkthrough: A massé is a shot played with the cue held almost upright, making the ball curve; 'this' supplies its first and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leader of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: Partner joins old singer somewhere in California

parts.note: a pal is a friend or partner
an alto is a singer with a low voice

explanation.surface: A partner teams up with a veteran vocalist on the West Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Palo Alto is a city in California's Silicon Valley.

clue.text: Bitter and excellent case of beer on the counter

parts.note: ace means excellent

indicators.note: counter means contrary, so these letters run against the way of the clue, upwards
case of means the outside letters, enclosing the rest

explanation.surface: A grumpy drinker gets a fine crate of beer at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives BR from beer, and 'on the counter' turns it to RB. The counter is not the bar but the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare word for sour or harsh in taste or manner.

clue.text: Plot next to street incorporating independent living accommodation

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: incorporating says the street abbreviation takes a letter inside

explanation.surface: A garden plot beside a road that includes self-contained housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room used for both living and sleeping, a British flat type.

clue.text: Bite-sized food partly makes us hiccup

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snack that gives us hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is Japanese vinegared rice with fish, served in mouthful-sized pieces.

clue.text: Cheese is fine to get gobbled up

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: gobbled means ate greedily

explanation.surface: Cheese is fine to be eaten greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only works as a reversal because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white, crumbly Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Where you may use a gun scope

definitions.text: Where you may use a gun
definitions.meaning: a firing ... is a place for shooting practice

explanation.surface: Choosing a gun sight for shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a shooting ground and also the extent or reach of something.

clue.text: Drills and cuts round base end of pillar

indicators.note: round says the cutting word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: excises means cuts out
E is the base of natural logarithms in maths

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter

explanation.surface: Construction work with power tools cutting around the foot of a column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts E and R (the last letter of pillar) inside EXCISES.
explanation.definitionFit: Drills and exercises are both routines of practice repeated to train.

clue.text: Detailed bill and letter from overseas

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a chit is a note of money owed, a bill

explanation.surface: An itemised invoice and a letter sent from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'itemised' but means de-tailed: CHIT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign letter.

clue.text: Crab meat is served over one type of grain

indicators.note: served means dished up, so these letters are presented in a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seafood dish laid over a portion of rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges CRAB MEAT IS with I.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grain aromatic rice from South Asia.
